evidence_quotes:
When the cooling
system pressure reaches approximately 15 psi (103 kPa), a valve in the surge tank cap
opens and lets excess pressure escape to the atmosphere.
statements.reason: It gives an approximate pressure, not an exact one.
statements.statement: The referenced material does not specify the exact pressure at which the surge-tank cap valve relieves pressure.

evidence_quotes:
If vehicle has been operating, use
extreme care to avoid being burned
when removing cooling system
radiator cap.
statements.reason: The warning explicitly gives this instruction.
statements.statement: After vehicle operation, the cooling-system PMCS warning instructs personnel to use extreme care to avoid burns when removing the radiator cap.

evidence_quotes:
If vehicle has been operating, use
extreme care to avoid being burned
when removing cooling system
radiator cap. Use heavy rags or gloves
to protect hands.
statements.reason: The warning explicitly gives this instruction.
statements.statement: After vehicle operation, the cooling-system PMCS warning instructs personnel to use heavy rags or gloves to protect hands.

evidence_quotes:
If vehicle has been operating, use
extreme care to avoid being burned
when removing cooling system
radiator cap. Use heavy rags or gloves
to protect hands. Turn radiator cap
only one-half turn counterclockwise
statements.reason: The warning explicitly specifies a one-half turn counterclockwise.
statements.statement: After vehicle operation, the cooling-system PMCS warning instructs personnel to turn the radiator cap only one-half turn counterclockwise.

evidence_quotes:
Turn radiator cap
only one-half turn counterclockwise
and allow pressure to be released
before fully removing cap.
statements.reason: The warning states this sequence directly.
statements.statement: After turning the radiator cap only one-half turn counterclockwise, the cooling-system PMCS warning instructs personnel to allow pressure to be released before fully removing the radiator cap.
